summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic abdominal pain and a history of syncope was admitted after fainting at her psychologist’s office, with a second syncopal episode noted in the ER two days prior. Her abdominal pain, localized to the left upper quadrant and worsened by eating, had led to a 10-pound unintentional weight loss and poor oral intake. She was admitted for pain control, nutritional support, and evaluation of recurrent syncope. A chest X-ray showed no acute disease, and urine culture revealed no infection. A PICC line was placed on hospital day 6 to initiate parenteral nutrition, supporting gradual improvement in oral intake and weight stabilization. She regained strength, tolerated a regular diet, and remained free of dizziness or syncope before discharge. Follow-up was arranged for ongoing GI evaluation, PICC line management, and assessment of persistent left breast pain. She was discharged home in stable condition with a plan for outpatient care.
